about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Marino, California
about.longDescription: San Marino is a quiet, tree-lined community, but collisions still happen on its streets. Public records show 64 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 91 people hurt and, notably, zero traffic deaths reported. Corridors like Huntington Drive, Los Robles Avenue, San Marino Avenue, and California Boulevard carry a good share of the city's daily traffic, and that's reflected in where collision reports tend to originate. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and paperwork can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm — that connects injured people in San Marino with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to find out where you stand, and reaching out early can help preserve evidence while memories and records are still fresh.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Real
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim in California, but claims against a government entity can require notice within as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. You aren't automatically shut out just because liability isn't one-sided.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That means compensation isn't limited to just medical bills and lost wages.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. This lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly rates or retainers while you're already dealing with medical costs.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in San Marino?
items.answer: Under California law, you typically have two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public property, the notice deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means partial responsibility reduces your compensation but doesn't bar you from recovering. An attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to cluster in San Marino?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Huntington Drive, Los Robles Avenue, San Marino Avenue, and California Boulevard are among the city's higher-volume corridors for reported collisions, with Thursdays around 3-5 p.m. showing more frequent reports. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service that helps injured people get in touch with an independent personal injury attorney. We don't provide legal representation ourselves, and there's no cost to use our service.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover compensation for you. There's no fee to get connected and discuss your situation.
